description: Straight-line distance alone picks the wrong venue: one candidate is genuinely nearer the outlying participant on a map, but the Ayalon and the railway run between them with no crossing on that stretch, while a nominally-farther candidate sits on a continuous arterial. This is the scenario that measures whether the Context Resolver's detour factor earns its place.

candidateVenues.name: Shapira Social
candidateVenues.note: 3.99 km from Gili in a straight line — nearer than Rothschild 12, and the better-rated venue. But the Ayalon and the railway run together between Shapira and Ramat Gan with no crossing on this stretch, so the approach is a good deal longer than the line suggests.

candidateVenues.name: Rothschild 12
candidateVenues.note: 4.25 km from Gili — slightly farther in a straight line, but reached from Ramat Gan along a continuous arterial with no barrier to work around.

expected.reasoning: Straight-line burdens (distance / toleranceKm, all tolerances 6 km, computed from the coordinates in this file): Shapira Social is [0.665 Gili, 0.376 Omer, 0.304 Tal] and Rothschild 12 is [0.708 Gili, 0.180 Omer, 0.171 Tal]. Leximin compares the worst-off participant first, so with no detour factor Shapira Social wins on 0.665 against 0.708 — and it is also the better-rated venue, so nothing else pulls the other way. A naive straight-line-only implementation is expected to get this one wrong; that gap is exactly what this scenario measures. Once the barrier between Shapira and Ramat Gan is priced in, Gili's burden at Shapira Social rises above hers at Rothschild 12 and the answer flips. The flip needs only that the Ramat Gan-Shapira detour factor exceed the Ramat Gan-Rothschild one by about 7% (4.247 / 3.988), so the scenario turns on the detour factor existing at all, not on its exact value: at a plausible 1.7 against 1.25 the vectors are [1.130, ...] and [0.885, ...] and Rothschild 12 wins comfortably. Note that the burden figure is a straight line with a correction factor, never a routed journey or a travel time (spec §5.4).
